messages.content:
Build a post-apocalyptic loot auto-battler. It's fully text-based, mobile-first but responsive enough to work with mouse and keyboard on desktop too. The player scavenges ruined locations for gear, equips it into a backpack, and fights auto-resolved battles where item stats and combos determine the outcome — no manual combat input, the build does the fighting.

For feel, borrow from Scavenge Wars the location-based looting loop: visiting a ruined location carries a real chance of an ambush that costs you items or energy, not just a guaranteed reward. Borrow from Backpack Brawl the equip mechanic: items slot into a limited backpack, and their combined properties (damage type, defense, rarity) roll up into an overall power level — call it "weight class" — that roughly predicts who wins a matchup, the way a heavier loadout usually beats a scrappier one.

Screens: Loot Locations, Backpack/Inventory, Arena, and a light Trader Outpost. Everything is text and UI, no camera or spatial rendering. Items and log entries are colored strictly by rarity tier — common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, and a distinct color reserved for one-of-a-kind items — so the player can read power level at a glance.

The v1 loop: player taps a loot location card (trigger). The game rolls the location event — either an item find or an ambush (action). On a find, the item drops into loose inventory; on a lost ambush, an item or energy is removed (result), logged as a colored text entry with a short flavor line (feedback). The player then drags or taps found items into backpack slots, watching their weight class total update live as they swap gear. From there they enter the Arena and pick an opponent from a pool of saved player builds — async, no live matchmaking, just battling against a snapshot of how someone else's backpack was equipped — with a handful of seeded NPC "veteran" builds mixed in early so the pool isn't empty on day one. The battle auto-resolves with a quick text log of exchanges, and the winner earns currency plus a chance at an item reward roughly matched to the tiers involved. Returning to the game after time away shows a short popup: how many battles happened passively against the player's own build while they were gone, wins, losses, and currency gained. The Trader Outpost is present but light for v1: simple buy and sell of items, plus one or two basic consumables like an energy-restoring recovery juice — no research system, no deep pricing economy yet.

Tone is dry post-apocalyptic scavenger humor — a legendary-tier item can absolutely be a paperclip. A good session looks like: loot a location, find something usable, adjust the backpack, run a couple of arena battles, and walk away with more currency or gear than you started with, watching your weight class creep upward over several sessions. There's no game-over state — losing a fight or an ambush just costs items or currency and the loop continues.

The game is built and compiles clean. Here's what's in:

**Spore Run** — plague & rot, dry deadpan, text-based auto-battler

**4 screens via bottom tab bar:**
- **RUINS** — 8 scavengeable locations (Fungal Grove, Overgrown Hospital, Research Lab sublevel, etc.), each with energy cost, ambush chance, and rarity range. Loot events show item found or ambush loss as a modal with dry flavor text. Log panel at the bottom tracks recent events colored by type/rarity.
- **LOADOUT** — 8 backpack slots displayed as a grid. Tap inventory item to equip to first free slot; tap equipped item to unequip. Weight class updates live with bio (×3 = +15% WC) and hazmat (×2 = +20 WC) combo callouts.
- **ARENA** — 6 seeded NPC opponents from Patient Zero (WC 16) up to The Collector (WC 655+). Shows weight class differential per opponent. Auto-battles resolve with a ~5-line text log; winner earns scrip and 30% chance of an item.
- **OUTPOST** — Random stock of 4 items + 2 always-available consumables (Recovery Juice restores energy, Scout's Map gives luck on next run). Sell loose inventory at 50% value.

**Systems:**
- 40 items across 6 rarity tiers (common → one-of-a-kind), plague-themed with dry descriptions. The Paperclip is legendary, as requested.
- Energy regenerates 1 per 30 min offline; passive arena battles fire every 2 hours (max 5 per session). Welcome-back popup on return.
- Full save persistence via RUN appStorage + localStorage fallback.
- Analytics on every major action (loot visit, ambush, battle win/loss, buy, sell, consumable use).

Clean. All four changes are in:

- **Palette** — secondary text bumped from `#6b7a6c` to `#a0c0a2` (sage-green, much more legible), card backgrounds from `#0b1a0d` to `#0e2010` for better contrast, borders from `#1a2e1c` to `#243e26`. Descriptions and log entries are now clearly readable.

- **Energy** — max raised to 20, starting with 18. Regenerates 1 per 5 minutes. The pip row is gone — replaced with a compact fill bar + `18/20 ⚡` label that color-shifts green → yellow → orange as energy drops.

- **Outpost auto-refresh** — shop stock refreshes automatically every 5 minutes. A live `0:00` countdown shows in the header. Manual refresh button removed.

- **Sell tab** — Outpost now has FOR SALE / SELL GEAR tabs at the top. The sell tab shows every inventory item (including consumables) with its sell price and a sell button. Tab label shows count of sellable items.

I'd say make it a bit more legible, but it's almost there.

The ruins, each location should also have a chance for extra loot to be found. The higher the tier, the higher the loot chance, but rolls lower loot in those spots than the main spot, so basically you cant get a one of a kind except in that first slot.

The loadout tab should feel a bit different, as its pretty basic right now. My original idea was to add a bar that the player would have to wait on, say a random time between 1 minute and 30 minutes, before adding that loot to their Safe House. Which is where the equipped items come into play, as its supposed to help fight off ambushes and attacks in the arena that may make you lose an item.

Some additional items that can be purchased or looted: different sizes of regen pots, small, med, large; an energy drink which temporarily boosts your regen from 5 minutes/energy to 1 minute/energy; a magnifying glass, which helps to research an item faster, also a difference in quality, 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes.

The on-of-a-kind items should feel insane to find, like 1 in 10,000+.

Their should be an active percenatge of total unique loot found, probably in that card.

Then lets add 100's of items. but only keep 10 on of a kind items to find, change them around if necessary. Actually lets make all 10 paperclips. The only paperclip you find is a one of a kind, and theres 10 left in the world. Said to be able to buy you whatever you want in this post - apoc world. They can be different names, but all are paperclips, like rusted paperclip, unfolded paperclip, bent paperclip, etc. Have an Explorer board that people can see which ones have been found, if any. from the 10 being something like half of a paperclip to 5 being unfolde paperclip to 1 being perfectly preserved paperclip. The lower the number, the more rare it actually is. 10 may be 1 in 10k but 5 is 1 in 30k and 1 is 1 in 50k.

Also, give players a chance to instantly scrap items when looting. Adds a single scrip, no matter the rarity. Also. We need to implement a menu with reutrn to title screen, a mute sound effects, a mute music, and a how to play. How to play should also be on the title screen, along with Explorer tab and play.

And each of the one of a kind shouldnt have a revealed name, it should be 3 questiuon marks uintil its found.

---

**Phase 3 complete.** Here's what changed:

**Legibility** — Secondary text bumped to `#bcd4bd`, descriptions are now noticeably clearer.

**130+ items** — Full item database expansion across all tiers. Common junk, uncommon salvage, rare military gear, epic experimental tech, legendary end-game items. The 10 unique items are now **only the 10 paperclips**, each with individual drop rates (1 in 10,000 → 1 in 50,000).

**Research Queue (LOADOUT tab)** — Found items go to the "Research Lab" with timers (common: 1-3 min, legendary: 20-30 min). Researched items move to "Safe House" when ready. Magnifying Glasses can accelerate any queued item. The screen now shows: Research Lab → Equipped → Safe House.

**Secondary loot** — Every successful scavenge can yield bonus items (auto-queued for research). Higher danger = higher chance + better caps. Extreme locations roll up to 3 bonus items (epic max). No paperclips from secondary slots.

**Scrap option** — Every loot modal now has a SCRAP (+1 scrip) button. Paperclips prompt a confirmation step before scrapping.

**New consumables** — Regen Pot S/M/L, Energy Drink (1/min regen for 30 min), Magnifying Glass in 3 sizes.

**Arena gear loss** — Losing a battle now carries a small chance of losing an equipped item (scales with WC disadvantage).

**Stats Card** — STATS button in Loadout shows battles, wins, scrip earned, scavenges, ambushes, and paperclip count.

**Menu** — In-game MENU button opens settings (How to Play, Explorer Board, Mute Music/SFX, Return to Title).

**Title screen** — HOW TO PLAY and EXPLORER BOARD buttons added alongside ENTER THE RUINS.

**Explorer Board** — Shows all 10 paperclips. Unfound ones show as ???. Drop rates listed. Accessible from both title and in-game menu.
